constraints: One font per text item: merged fallback fonts and per-run baseline alignment from hhea metrics.

narrative.overview:
The whole window is a sheet of Chinese proofreading paper laid on a desk: cool white stock, a printed green grid, and one vermilion pen that only ever marks deletions. This is not an editing suite. It refuses the NLE cockpit (dark grey, orange accent, many tracks) and the light SaaS dashboard (rounded cards, soft shadows). Cutting a sponsor segment reads as striking a passage from a manuscript: the document stays the same document, a passage is marked out, and the margin note says how much is gone.

The video frame sits in an ink well, a black field with a dark border, so the eye's local surround stays dark while the rest of the desk stays paper. Density is that of a working document: three fixed columns (cache list, sheet, "this one" inspector), quiet hairlines, and numerals set in a condensed tabular face so running clocks never jitter. Every surface is flat; structure comes from tone (paper, shade, crease) and 1px lines, never from lift.

The system lives in one file, `bili_look.py`. Colours, the type scale, font roles and every theme are defined there; `bili_gui.py` only references them. Only the light paper theme exists. A dark theme is a deferred, open decision; if it comes, it swaps the palette in that file and nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-toned flat surfaces; depth by tone and hairline only.
One accent, vermilion, with exactly two meanings: will be removed, and irreversible.
The 刪除號 (deletion mark) on the 稿紙 grid timeline is the signature.
Serif headings, sans body, condensed tabular numerals for every time and byte count.
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero gradient.
Everything scales with the five-step user font size through `px()`; layout reflows rather than just enlarging text.

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: Vermilion means "this will be removed" or "this cannot be undone". Nothing else is red: not errors, not warnings, not links, not focus. A missing dependency is shown in ink plus bold; a caution is ochre. Every extra red dilutes the deletion mark.

rules.name: The One Red Block Rule
rules.body: In the main window the only filled vermilion block is the write action in the inspector. Other vermilion is line, text or tint.

rules.name: The Not By Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every coloured state also carries text or shape: the strike has hooks and a 「刪」 label, the status square has a label, unsupported rows say why.

rules.name: The Steady Clock Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes while playing or that is compared in a column (times, bytes, counts) is set in the tabular numeral face. Proportional digits are a defect.

rules.name: The Mixed-Run Rule
rules.body: A Dear PyGui text item has one font, so mixed CJK and numeral runs are separate items aligned on a shared baseline computed from each font's hhea metrics. Do not fake alignment with manual nudges.

rules.name: Open: the numeral family
rules.body: The direction contract names Barlow Semi Condensed for numerals. The build uses Bahnschrift SemiCondensed because Barlow would have to be downloaded and bundled, which has not been approved. This is unresolved; the user will decide. Do not swap it either way without that decision.

rules.name: The Scale Everything Rule
rules.body: Every dimension goes through `px()` and the theme is rebuilt on a font-size change; the timeline geometry is recomputed too. A hard-coded physical pixel is a bug, except deliberate 1px hairlines.

rules.name: The Paper Has No Shadows Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs separation, use a tone step or a 1px line.

rules.name: The Snapped Truth Rule
rules.body: Every number about a cut is the snapped value, the one that will actually be removed: strike label, cut list 起 / 迄 / 實際刪, inspector, confirm dialog. Never show the requested value where the removed value belongs. Durations use `fmt_dur`, which rounds to the second, so 原長 minus 移除 equals 新長.

rules.name: The Flush Text Rule
rules.body: Dear PyGui pushes text down by FramePadding.y. Containers whose children are positioned by coordinate (bar, list pane, footer, key-value, cut list, log) zero it, so a coordinate is where the glyph actually sits.

dos: **Do** keep every colour, size, font role and theme in `bili_look.py`; a future dark theme swaps that palette only.
**Do** use vermilion only for what will be removed and for irreversible actions (寫入手機, 還原到手機, 備份並寫入).
**Do** show warnings in ochre and missing or failed states in ink plus bold.
**Do** set every time, byte count and count in the tabular numeral face.
**Do** show snapped, actually-removed values everywhere and round durations with `fmt_dur`.
**Do** draw cut points on fragment grid lines and state the grid unit (一格＝k 個 fragment) whenever k > 1.
**Do** pass every dimension through `px()` and verify at the largest user font size.
**Do** draw hairlines as 1x1 tinted images or half-pixel lines.
donts: **Don't** use vermilion for errors, warnings, links, focus or decoration.
**Don't** round a corner, cast a shadow or use a gradient.
**Don't** use dashed borders or rely on letter-spacing; Dear PyGui has neither.
**Don't** use proportional digits for anything that ticks or is compared in a column.
**Don't** put the video frame on paper; it lives in the ink well.
**Don't** swap Bahnschrift for Barlow Semi Condensed, or the reverse, until the user decides.
**Don't** add a second theme until the light / dark decision is made.
